ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

Alert: search-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 02:43 UTC)
Alerting service: search
Alert time: 2026-03-11T02:43:00Z
Data available from 2026-03-11T01:00:00Z to 2026-03-11T04:00:00Z

Evidence so far (the latest results are steps 4 onwards):
Step 1: metrics_query {"aggregation": "mean", "end": "2026-03-11T04:00:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "search", "start": "2026-03-11T01:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check error rate trends for the search service over time.)
  Result: M-050: Change detected at 2026-03-11T02:40:00Z: mean 0.4 before, 19.57 after (169.3 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-050] search.error_rate_pct from 2026-03-11T01:00:00Z to 2026-03-11T03:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.2 max=19.73 mean=8.92 last=19.59; mean=8.92. Change detected at 2026-03-11T02:40:00Z: mean 0.4 before, 19.57 after (169.3 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-03-11T01:05:00Z = 0.2 (lowest); 2026-03-11T02:40:00Z = 19.47 (first point after the change); 2026-03-11T03:35:00Z = 19.73 (peak); 2026-03-11T03:55:00Z = 19.59 (last).
Step 2: metrics_query {"aggregation": "mean", "end": "2026-03-11T04:00:00Z", "metric": "latency_p99_ms", "service": "search", "start": "2026-03-11T01:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check latency p99 trends for the search service.)
  Result: M-051: Change detected at 2026-03-11T02:25:00Z: mean 149.49 before, 5073.18 after (595.2 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-051] search.latency_p99_ms from 2026-03-11T01:00:00Z to 2026-03-11T03:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=135.69 max=6197.23 mean=2748.11 last=6183.92; mean=2748.11. Change detected at 2026-03-11T02:25:00Z: mean 149.49 before, 5073.18 after (595.2 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-03-11T01:15:00Z = 135.69 (lowest); 2026-03-11T02:25:00Z = 898.48 (first point after the change); 2026-03-11T03:20:00Z = 6197.23 (peak); 2026-03-11T03:55:00Z = 6183.92 (last).
Step 3: metrics_query {"aggregation": "mean", "end": "2026-03-11T04:00:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "search", "start": "2026-03-11T01:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check database connection pool usage for search service.)
  Result: M-048: Change detected at 2026-03-11T01:15:00Z: mean 27.2 before, 64.46 after (15.9 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-048] search.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-03-11T01:00:00Z to 2026-03-11T03:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=23.89 max=100 mean=61.35 last=96.41; mean=61.35. Change detected at 2026-03-11T01:15:00Z: mean 27.2 before, 64.46 after (15.9 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-03-11T01:15:00Z = 35.9 (first point after the change); 2026-03-11T01:25:00Z = 23.89 (lowest); 2026-03-11T02:55:00Z = 100 (peak); 2026-03-11T03:55:00Z = 96.41 (last).
Step 4: metrics_query {"aggregation": "mean", "end": "2026-03-11T04:00:00Z", "metric": "cache_hit_ratio_pct", "service": "search", "start": "2026-03-11T01:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if cache hit ratio dropped or if cache is down, which could explain database connection pool exhaustion.)
  Result: M-046: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-046] search.cache_hit_ratio_pct from 2026-03-11T01:00:00Z to 2026-03-11T03:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=90.43 max=94.75 mean=92.89 last=93.73; mean=92.89. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-03-11T01:40:00Z = 94.75 (peak); 2026-03-11T03:10:00Z = 90.43 (lowest); 2026-03-11T03:55:00Z = 93.73 (last).
Step 5: log_search {"end": "2026-03-11T02:50:00Z", "limit": 30, "query": "pool connection database timeout slow query error", "service": "search", "start": "2026-03-11T02:20:00Z"} (asked because: Search logs around the start of the latency spike for database connection pool issues or slow query warnings.)
  Result: 5 matching log lines.
  [L-0255] 2026-03-11T02:34:22Z search WARN slow request took 387ms path=/api/v1/search
  [L-0271] 2026-03-11T02:40:12Z search ERROR HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms (total=50, active=50, idle=0, waiting=50)
  [L-0277] 2026-03-11T02:40:43Z search ERROR Unable to acquire JDBC Connection url=jdbc:postgresql://search_app:[SECRET_2]@search-db-1:5432/search
  [L-0282] 2026-03-11T02:41:36Z search WARN connection pool exhausted: max=50 active=50 waiting=63
  [L-0305] 2026-03-11T02:48:15Z search WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m

Previous hypotheses:
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: Database connection pool utilization reached 100% alongside high p99 latency and increasing error rates. (evidence: M-048, M-050, M-051)
- slow_query_missing_index: Queries becoming slow can cause connections to stay active longer in the pool, leading to connection pool exhaustion, high latency, and errors. (evidence: M-048, M-050, M-051)
- cache_stampede_outage: A cache failure could cause a surge of direct database traffic, saturating the connection pool and increasing latency. (evidence: M-048, M-050, M-051)
